Class FarRest

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.FarRest
public final class FarRest extends Object
A steady hand on an opponent that is far away. With the opponent on screen and a long way off, the camera is not the network's to move: it is brought onto the opponent and kept there by AimRule's plain steering, which turns towards it by a share of what is left on every tick, follows it smoothly while it walks across the picture, and rests while it does not.

Why it is a rule. The hand model (AimMotor) starts a turn at a degree a tick and no less, so the smallest correction it can make from rest is a good degree. Twenty blocks away the whole opponent is a degree and a half wide. The network, paid for a crosshair on the opponent, went on correcting there, each correction as large as the target, one way and then the other: the picture shook. Nothing can be hit from there; what a player does is keep the opponent about in the middle of the screen with a quiet hand.

It goes by what the network itself is shown: how tall the opponent is on screen, which says how far away it is, and where it is from the crosshair.
